signals.name: Alphabet
signals.label: Broadest whale consensus of the cycle, but Congress just split on it
signals.detail: Berkshire's Q2-2026 13F (filed mid-Aug 2026, Abel's second as CEO) showed the firm a net equity buyer for the first time in 3+ years, driven by a ~$17B further Alphabet add that made GOOGL a top-3 Berkshire holding; Soros and Druckenmiller (new ~$120M/336,300-share stake) are also long. But the congressional picture just cracked: Rep. David Taylor bought GOOGL on 11 Aug, while Rep. Michael Rulli SOLD GOOGL on 24 Aug -- almost exactly two months after buying an overlapping block in late June (a round trip that may have lost him money on the shares).
signals.takeaway: Institutional/macro-whale conviction on Alphabet remains about as broad as any single name gets, but the freshest congressional data point is a sale, not a buy -- worth watching whether Rulli's move is noise (he trades constantly) or an early tell.

signals.name: Amazon
signals.label: Two macro whales converging on the same hyperscaler bet
signals.detail: Duquesne/Druckenmiller's Q2-2026 13F showed Amazon common shares up from 45,800 to 541,600 (10x+) plus new call options on 459,300 more shares (~$239M combined exposure) -- funded in part by fully exiting Micron, Intel, Broadcom, Lattice and Coherent. Separately, Appaloosa/Tepper's Q2-2026 filing (reported alongside a China-holdings reshuffle) was described in coverage as 'betting big on Amazon and AI power infrastructure.'
signals.takeaway: Two macro funds that just cut very different things (chip/photonics names for Druckenmiller, Chinese e-commerce for Tepper) both rotated the proceeds toward Amazon -- a genuine cross-fund convergence on the hyperscaler/compute layer over component suppliers.

signals.name: Micron
signals.label: Whale conviction still fractured, unresolved into a second quarter
signals.detail: Soros Fund Management's Q2-2026 13F (filed 14 Aug 2026) increased Micron nearly eightfold (2,824 -> 22,422 shares, ~$25.9M), while Duquesne/Druckenmiller's same-quarter filing showed a full exit of Micron alongside Intel, Broadcom, Lattice and Coherent -- the opposite side of the same trade.
signals.takeaway: This is the same memory-chip split flagged last cycle, now confirmed to have persisted through Q2 rather than converging -- a genuine two-sided whale book on Micron specifically, not a consensus name.

signals.name: Cerebras Systems
signals.label: AI-silicon diversification trade, now shared by two funds
signals.detail: Tiger Global's Q2-2026 13F showed its largest new stake was Cerebras (~$660M) alongside a new ~$392M AMD position, part of a broader move from 54 to 46 total positions (17 exits, 9 new). Duquesne/Druckenmiller's same-quarter filing also opened a new AMD stake even while exiting legacy chip names entirely.
signals.takeaway: Two macro/growth funds are independently rotating down the AI stack into chip challengers (Cerebras) and AMD rather than staying concentrated in Nvidia -- an emerging 'AI-silicon diversification' theme distinct from the mega-cap AI trade.

signals.name: CrowdStrike
signals.label: A House Intel cyber-subcommittee member just bought a cybersecurity basket
signals.detail: Rep. Josh Gottheimer, ranking member of the House Intelligence Committee's NSA & Cyber Subcommittee, disclosed buying CrowdStrike (15 Jul), Palo Alto Networks (16 Jul) and SailPoint (20 Jul) within days of each other, filed 10 Aug 2026 in the same batch as his Alphabet buy and several industrial/tech trims.
signals.takeaway: A concentrated, committee-relevant cybersecurity basket from a single well-placed member is a narrower signal than a multi-investor convergence, but the sector clustering and his oversight role make it worth tracking rather than treating as routine account-manager noise.

signals.name: Xiaomi
signals.label: Institutional and founder buying aligned on the same book holding
signals.detail: HKEX Disclosure-of-Interest filings show BlackRock's fund complex has been almost continuously adding to its ~5% notifiable Xiaomi stake through August 2026 (latest confirmed 24 Aug, +27,917,906 shares), while founders Lei Jun (Chairman/CEO) and Lin Bin (President) both increased their own stated interests in an 11 Aug filing -- no per-share price was disclosed in either filing set.
signals.takeaway: A rare alignment of passive/institutional flow and founder-level insider activity on the same name in the owner's HKEX book, though the founder filings' scale and same-day timing look more like a scheduled equity-incentive event than a discretionary market buy.
